articles.summary: A Black Friday 2026 acontece em 27 de novembro e especialistas recomendam monitorar preços agora para garantir descontos reais e fugir de falsas promoções.
articles.body:
A Black Friday 2026 vai acontecer na semana do dia 27 de novembro .

Mas todo mundo já sabe que nem todo desconto é real, o que já levou o período a ser apelidado até de "Black Fraude".

Para não cair em ciladas , a primeira dica é começar a acompanhar o preço dos produtos quanto antes.

No final de agosto, uma pesquisa do Google indicou que 48% dos consumidores chegarão à Black Friday com a lista de compras definida e 41% pretendem gastar mais que em 2025.

Diz a pesquisa que 15% dos entrevistados "dizem que vão usar a inteligência artificial para pesquisar, monitorar preços e avaliar" se uma promoção compensa.

Além disso, 60% dos pesquisados consideram a Black Friday a única data que vale a pena para comprar itens de alto valor.

Como não cair em ciladas na Black Friday?

O Procon-SP recomenda iniciar agora a pesquisa pelos produtos desejados na Black Friday para o consumidor conhecer os valores médios, já que não existe tabelamento de preços no Brasil.

articles.title: Renan Santos propõe infraestrutura e segurança jurídica para o agro | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à presidência da República pelo Missão se reuniu com apoiadores na Avenida Nove de Julho na noite desta quinta-feira (24).
articles.summary: Em Ribeirão Preto, o candidato Renan Santos apresentou propostas de infraestrutura e segurança jurídica para fortalecer o agronegócio brasileiro.
articles.body:
Renan Santos (Missão), candidato à presidência da República, durante evento da campanha em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Alexandre David/EPTV

O candidato à Presidência da República Renan Santos (Missão) afirmou nesta quinta-feira (24), durante agenda de campanha em Ribeirão Preto (SP), que pretende ampliar investimentos em infraestrutura e promover medidas para dar, segundo ele, mais segurança jurídica aos produtores rurais.

Entre as propostas citadas pelo candidato estão a construção de ferrovias e estradas e a ampliação da oferta de energia, com a implantação de novas usinas hidrelétricas. Também defendeu melhores condições para a construção de silos e estruturas de armazenamento.

Renan se reuniu com apoiadores na Avenida Nove de Julho. Ribeirão Preto foi a última parada do candidato em uma série de compromissos de campanha no interior de São Paulo nesta quinta-feira. Antes, ele passou por Piracicaba (SP) e São Carlos (SP).

Ao falar sobre o agronegócio, Renan avaliou que a infraestrutura disponível no país é insuficiente para atender às necessidades do setor e citou como prioridades as áreas de energia e transporte.

“Investimento em infraestrutura. A infraestrutura é precária. Investimento em infraestrutura tanto para energia quanto ferrovia, estrada e rodagem.”

Na avaliação do candidato, o agronegócio já dispõe de mecanismos de financiamento, mas ainda enfrenta dificuldades relacionadas à infraestrutura logística para melhorar o escoamento da produção. Ele mencionou a necessidade de ampliar estruturas de armazenamento, como silos, próximas às áreas produtoras.

O candidato defendeu a construção de novas usinas hidrelétricas com grandes reservatórios. Segundo ele, a medida permitiria ampliar a geração de energia para atividades do agronegócio, especialmente aquelas que dependem de sistemas de irrigação.

Renan afirmou que considera o custo da energia um dos problemas enfrentados pelos produtores e disse que pretende aumentar a capacidade de geração no país.

“Boa parte do agro brasileiro depende de energia, especialmente para irrigação. A energia do Brasil está cada vez mais cara e tende a ficar mais cara. Nós precisamos de novas usinas hidrelétricas feitas com grandes reservas.”

Outro ponto defendido por Renan foi o que chamou de maior “segurança jurídica” para os produtores rurais. Segundo ele, isso envolve garantir a manutenção da propriedade da terra e reduzir obstáculos à implantação de obras de infraestrutura.

“Ele precisa agora, e é um pedido de todo o agro, incluindo o daqui, segurança jurídica. Segurança jurídica para manutenção da propriedade sobre as suas próprias terras, criação de infraestrutura ao redor deles, de silos, armazenamento, ferrovia e rodovia.”

Renan também criticou a atuação de organizações não governamentais em processos envolvendo obras de infraestrutura. Segundo o candidato, há casos em que a interferência dessas entidades provoca a paralisação de projetos.

O candidato permanece na região nesta sexta-feira (25), quando cumpre agenda pela manhã em Franca (SP).

articles.title: Renan Santos, candidato à Presidência pelo Missão, tem agenda no interior de São Paulo | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato disse que pretende investir em educação e esporte para tirar jovens da criminalidade.
articles.summary: Candidato disse que pretende investir em educação e esporte para tirar jovens da criminalidade.
articles.body:
O candidato Renan Santos , do Missão , teve agenda no interior de São Paulo.

Renan Santos começou o dia em Piracicaba. Caminhou pelo Mercado Municipal e discursou para eleitores. Na sequência, seguiu para São Carlos. O candidato se encontrou com apoiadores e falou com jornalistas. Renan Santos aumentar o número de cursos nas áreas de tecnologia, inteligência artificial e geologia nas universidades publicas e investir em educação e esporte para tirar jovens da criminalidade:

“Forma a disciplina, a autoconsciência dos mais jovens. Existe uma correlação direta entre esporte e autodisciplina, esporte e saúde. E o problema de enfrentamento ao crime organizado é transformar os esportes em formas de disciplina e de correção, utilizando não só o professor com autoridade dessa vez e o esporte como instrumento que pega um menino problemático e o transforma em um atleta”.

Depois do almoço, o candidato à Presidência Renan Santos cumprimentou alguns apoiadores e seguiu para Ribeirão Preto, conhecida como a capital do agronegócio, para mais compromissos de campanha.

articles.title: 7-year-old girl dies after collapsing in class amid loud DJ procession in UP; 2 arrested
articles.summary: Balrampur police arrest DJ owner, operator after 7-year-old student dies during Ganpati immersion; FIR filed, equipment seized, cause unconfirmed.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Balrampur police on Wednesday night arrested a DJ owner and an operator after a seven-year-old student died allegedly because of loud DJ music being played near her school during a Ganesh idol immersion procession on Tuesday.Police arrested Chandra Prakash Verma, owner of Balaji Hightech DJ, and Rampal Saini, the DJ operator, while Shailendra Kumar Yadav, in charge of Mewalal police outpost, was suspended. Santosh Mishra, Kotwali Nagar inspector, was also issued a show-cause notice for negligence.An FIR was registered at Kotwali Nagar police station on the complaint of school manager Ashish Kumar Upadhyay, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 223 (disobedience to public servant) of BNS.Police also seized the pickup vehicle, the DJ sound system and other equipment allegedly used during the procession.A senior police officer said the deceased was attending classes as usual when she collapsed at around 10.58 am. Teachers immediately attended to her. She briefly regained her posture but collapsed again shortly afterwards and did not respond to attempts to revive her. She was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead.At the time of the incident, a Ganpati immersion procession was passing near the school with a DJ system. A teacher, Ikra Khan, told investigators that the DJ sound had intensified and vibrations could be felt inside the classroom around the time Vaishnavi fell ill.Police are scanning the CCTV footage from the classroom to establish the sequence of events.However, police have not established that the DJ sound caused the girl’s death. The child was not subjected to a post-mortem examination, making it difficult to medically determine the exact cause of death.Following the incident, police held a meeting with DJ operators and directed them not to play DJs after 10 pm, avoid excessive use of heavy bass and refrain from using unusually tall DJ setups.Police said excessive noise can adversely affect children, the elderly, patients and students.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Aaya Ram, gaya Ram, phir aaya Ram: SC dismisses Danam Nagender's plea, sets stage for high-octane assembly by-election
articles.summary: Supreme Court upholds Telangana HC order disqualifying Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender under anti-defection law, clearing way for by-election.
articles.body: Hyderabad: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the Telangana high court’s order disqualifying Danam Nagender as the Khairatabad MLA, setting the stage for a high-octane assembly by-election in Telangana.Dismissing Nagender’s special leave petition, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that the high court had rightly interpreted the law on defections and that there was no ground to interfere in the order.“Your case is ‘Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram, phir Aaya Ram’,” Justice Bagchi remarked, adding, “You had a fixed deposit as MLA. You tried for the share market as an MP, and now you lost the fixed deposit.”Nagender had won the Khairatabad assembly seat on a BRS ticket in Dec 2023 and later contested and lost the Secunderabad Lok Sabha election on a Congress ticket in March 2024. The high court had on Sept 18 disqualified him as a member of the Telangana assembly under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.The high court, while disposing of petitions filed by BJP floor leader in the assembly Alleti Maheshwar Reddy and BRS MLA Padi Kaushik Reddy, had also set aside the assembly speaker’s decision dismissing disqualification petitions against Nagender. With this, Nagender stood disqualified as an MLA from April 23, 2024 — the day on which he filed nomination papers for the Lok Sabha elections.Nagender’s SLP had been mentioned before the CJI bench on Sept 21. Senior Counsel Mukul Rohatgi, while appearing for Nagender, had sought an urgent hearing contending that any delay could result in the Election Commission issuing a by-poll notification for the Khairatabad assembly constituency. Moreover, the MLA being disqualified, the public would suffer and welfare programmes would also be affected.On Thursday, Rohatgi submitted that there was a provision in the Tenth Schedule to condone the act of a member giving up party membership. “Ghar Wapasi?” Justice Bagchi asked.However, BRS insisted that they had not taken Nagender back into its fold. The counsel for Kaushik Reddy said that the party had not condoned Nagender’s acts, and underscored that it was the BRS member who filed the disqualification petition before the assembly speaker.Taking note of the submissions, the bench dismissed the Nagender’s plea.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: ‘Fed up’, Calcutta high court tells Election Commission it should be impartial
articles.summary: Calcutta High Court rebukes Election Commission for allotting ISF’s ‘envelope’ symbol to Democratic Trinamool Congress for Oct 6 bypoll; hearing Friday.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Calcutta High Court on Thursday pulled up Election Commission for allotting ‘envelope’ symbol — used by Indian Secular Front in the 2026 assembly election — to Democratic Trinamool Congress for the Oct 6 bypoll, and berated the commission for “creating trouble” and forcing parties to start legal proceedings thereby “burdening” the court.“Really fed up with the authority.... Once the elections start, you start creating trouble. Then parties come to court, putting burden on the court,” the high court told EC’s counsel.“Authorities should act impartially and fairly,” Justice Krishna Rao told the poll panel and questioned why it had to choose ‘envelope’ from among 183 symbols to give to another party. The angry judge asked why EC was getting into disputes and ruffling parties to create legal proceedings. “Is this the way it works?” he asked.Nawsad Siddiqui-led ISF, which won the Bhangar seat in assembly elections, had moved the high court praying for a direction to EC to freeze the ‘envelope’ symbol. After allotting ‘envelope’ to Democratic Trinamool Congress, EC gave ISF the ‘almirah’ symbol for the bypolls.“Our voters will be confused. We fought the 2026 assembly election using ‘envelope’ and we are also contesting the bypolls,” ISF’s counsel and senior advocate Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharyya told the judge.EC’s counsel argued that ISF is a registered unrecognised party and such parties do not have reserved symbols. ISF was given ‘envelope’ twice, the last being the 2026 assembly election. ISF countered that the by-election was a continuation of the assembly election.When Justice Rao asked if ISF had applied for a symbol for the bypoll, its counsel said there was no new notification asking political parties to submit Form 10b for allotment of symbols.Justice Rao said, “If you (EC) find that just four months back the symbol was used by one political party, for the by-election why did you choose that particular symbol? You could have kept it reserved like the others. articles.title: Carro cai em buraco após rompimento de encanamento em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na manhã de sexta-feira (25) e ninguém se feriu.
articles.summary: Carro cai em buraco no bairro Mansões Santo Antônio após rompimento de encanamento; Sanasa realiza reparo emergencial e não há feridos no local.
articles.body:
Carro cai em buraco após rompimento de encanamento em Campinas — Foto: Johnny Inselsperger/EPTV

Um carro caiu em um buraco aberto após o rompimento de um encanamento na manhã desta sexta-feira (25), no cruzamento das ruas Hortênsias e Girassol, no bairro Mansões Santo Antônio, em Campinas (SP). Ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo a Empresa Municipal de Desenvolvimento de Campinas (Emdec), o rompimento ocorreu enquanto o veículo passava pelo local . Um guincho foi acionado para retirar o carro, e não houve impacto no trânsito.

Em nota, a Sociedade de Abastecimento de Água e Saneamento (Sanasa) informou que duas equipes foram mobilizadas, sendo uma para fechar os registros da rede e outra para realizar um reparo emergencial na rede de distribuição de água.

articles.title: ‘Remember the beepers?’: Netanyahu flashes pagers at UN, recalls deadly Hezbollah operation - video
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held up a pager during his address to the UN General Assembly on Thursday as he defended Israel’s military
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held up a pager during his address to the UN General Assembly on Thursday as he defended Israel’s military operations against Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran, while dozens of delegates walked out of the hall as he began speaking.Netanyahu used the device to reference Israel’s September 2024 pager operation against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon. He also defended Israel’s war against Iran, saying the decision to attack its nuclear facilities “was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make.”The speech was repeatedly disrupted by the departure of delegates, with many seats left empty as Netanyahu took the podium. UN General Assembly President Khalilur Rahman repeatedly called for order.“If there are any other moral cowards who have not yet left the hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said.Netanyahu also rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, calling such claims “the biggest lie of the century.” Israel has rejected allegations of genocide and war crimes in Gaza.Netanyahu holds up pager in Hezbollah referenceDuring his speech, Netanyahu held up a pager while recalling Israel’s September 17, 2024, operation targeting Hezbollah.Thousands of pagers distributed among Hezbollah members exploded in Lebanon and Syria. The attack killed 12 people, including two children, and wounded more than 3,000, according to the figures cited in the speech coverage.Netanyahu used the operation to underline his claim that Israel had inflicted major setbacks on Hezbollah and other groups fighting Israel."Israel struck Hamas, we struck Hezbollah. Do you remember the pagers?" Netanyahu said.He also described the wider conflict as a “seven-front war”, listing Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, Iran, militias in Iraq, militias in Syria and Palestinian militants in the West Bank.Netanyahu said in his speech at the UN that "in the last three years, our heroic soldiers have fought a war on seven fronts. Do you know of any other country the size of New Jersey that can fight for three years on seven fronts?" Netanyahu continued: "They organized to erase us from the face of the Earth. Instead of collapsing, we delivered devastating blows to all of them with our great American friends and crushed the Iranian army and its nuclear facilities." He held up a pager and said: "Israel struck Hamas, we struck Hezbollah. Do you remember the pagers?""Netanyahu calls Iran strike an easy decisionNetanyahu strongly defended Israel’s military campaign against Iran, including strikes on its nuclear facilities."Netanyahu, his voice rising in emphasis, said attacking Iran “was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make” and denounced as “moral cowards” a mass of delegates who walked out of the U.N. General Assembly when he took the podium to speak."He said Israel’s military actions had also benefited countries that publicly criticised its operations.“In defending itself, Israel is also also defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall,” Netanyahu said. “In fact, I want you to know that many of their leaders even thank us privately for taking out Iran’s nukes.”Netanyahu described Iran as a “murderous dictatorship” and said Israel had sought to prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons.“I vowed to prevent Iran's murderous dictatorship from developing atomic bombs, nuclear weapons aimed at destroying Israel, nuclear weapons that could threaten the entire world," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump, Xi exchange warm words before White House state dinner: What they said
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping exchanged warm remarks before joining guests for a White House state dinner, with both leaders
articles.body: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping exchanged warm remarks before joining guests for a White House state dinner, with both leaders speaking about the importance of ties between the two countries and their hopes for a more stable relationship.Trump welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the White House alongside first lady Melania Trump. The state dinner in the East Room brought together senior US officials, business leaders and executives from some of America's biggest technology companies.In his remarks, Trump said the two leaders represented different political systems but stressed the enduring ties between the American and Chinese peoples."As the leaders of our two nations, President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better...Together, we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations"Trump also welcomed Xi and Peng to Washington, recalling his own visit to Beijing and saying the United States hoped to extend the same hospitality to the Chinese delegation."This is a great honor. President Xi, Madam Peng and members of the Chinese delegation, Melania and I are delighted to welcome you once again to the White House. You are truly outstanding, amazing people. The hospitality of the Chinese people was on full display during my visit to Beijing. We hope to show you the same honor as you returned to Washington for the first time in over a decade..."Xi calls for a new chapter in US-China tiesXi also struck a conciliatory tone, using the imagery of a flowing river and flowers to describe the relationship between the two countries."Like a river that never stops flowing, history never stands still. The friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise. Let us join hands and move forward side by side. Together, let us nurture the beautiful flowers of Sino-US friendship. Together, let us write a new chapter in our friendly relations"Xi referred to Trump's visit to China earlier this year and said the two presidents had agreed to work toward a constructive relationship based on strategic stability."In May this year, President Trump paid a successful visit to China at my invitation. We agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. During the visit, President Trump warmly invited me to visit the United States, and I have come as promised. In less than half a year, the Chinese and American presidents have exchanged state visits, making history in our bilateral engagement. Today, President Trump and I had sincere and in-depth exchanges and reached a common understanding on many issues. This has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and provided new strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations"Xi also thanked Trump and Melania Trump for their hospitality during the visit."Thank you, Mr. President and Mrs. Trump, for extending to my wife and me your gracious hospitality and thoughtful arrangements. You and Mrs. Trump have made many special arrangements for our visit, all prepared with meticulous care and consideration in every detail. You make us feel truly at home. I would also like to extend my sincere greetings to Americans from all sectors of society who care about China-U.S. relations and support the further growth of our bilateral ties..."Trump presents Xi with bald eagle giftTrump also presented Xi with a gift made by an American artist, saying it had been designed in collaboration with Melania Trump. He described the bald eagle as a national symbol of the United States."I present President Xi with a gift made by an extraordinary American artist, one of the greatest in the world and designed in personal collaboration with Melania and myself. The bald eagle is a national symbol of the United States and an embodiment of the free and soaring spirit of America. We hope it'll find a nice place, a wonderful place in Beijing..."Tech leaders, CEOs among state dinner guestsThe dinner brought together prominent figures from the technology, finance and media sectors. Among those attending were Apple CEO Tim Cook, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Zoom CEO Eric Yuan and TikTok investor Jeff Yass.The guest list also included senior figures from the financial sector, including the CEOs of JPMorgan Chase, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs. LVMH CEO Bernard Arnault and Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla were also present.Fox News hosts Bret Baier and Laura Ingraham, along with Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison, were among the media and entertainment figures attending.The dinner was held in the White House East Room. The White House said the menu combined American ingredients with Chinese influences and included a toast with Schramsberg Blanc de Noir, followed by dishes including sea bass and a dessert featuring White House honey.The state dinner came as Washington and Beijing continued to manage disagreements over trade, Taiwan, artificial intelligence, advanced technology and critical minerals. The public warmth displayed by Trump and Xi contrasted with the range of issues still shaping the US-China relationship.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: IIT-Bombay delays tests as faculty calls for 'student-friendly' SOP on handling exam misconduct
articles.summary: MUMABAI: IIT-Bombay has postponed a set of mid-semester exams to give a committee time to frame an SOP and revise rules to handle academic misconduct.
articles.body: MUMABAI: IIT-Bombay has po­stponed a set of mid-sem­ester exams to give a committee time to frame an SOP and revise rules to han­dle academic misconduct.Last Saturday, a profess­or was named in an FIR by the par­ents of a 2nd-year student who committed suicide.Faculty members have demanded a clear standard operating procedure (SOP) that spells out, step by step, how invigilators should deal with students suspected of exam malpractice. The tests sched­u­led for Sept 26-27 will now be held on Oct 10-11, with the tim­etable remaining unchanged, stud­ents were told Thursday.A communication sent by Siddhant Gupta, general sec­retary, academic affairs (UG), said the postponement is intended to give the new comm­ittee, which has equal student representation, time to draw up a “clear and student-frie­ndly” SOP for invigilators and revise the rules govern­ing academic misconduct.The move assumes significance amid the debate on how students accused of exam violations are dealt with on campus and whether existing procedures leave too much discretion to individual faculty members or invigilators.Faculty members have specifically emphasised the need for detailed instructi­ons on how examinations are to be conducted and how suspected cases of misconduct should be handled. The proposed SOP is expected to lay down the procedure to be followed at every stage, from the point at which an invigilator suspects a violation to the subsequent action against the student.“Faculty have emphasised the need for clear, step-by-step instructions on conducting examinations and handling incidents of suspected academic misconduct, including the procedure and actions to be followed at each stage,” the letter said.The institute has said the objective is to ensure that examinations are conducted in a fair and consistent manner, while also giving due consideration to students’ concerns. Student stakeholders were consulted before the exams were postponed, the communication said.The revised SOP and academic misconduct rules will not come into force immediately. These will first be placed before the IIT-B senate for approval, said the letter sent to campus residents. “The exercise could lead to a more standardised framework for dealing with suspected examination violations, particularly by defining what an invigilator can do at the examination hall, what must be documented, and what procedure should follow before further disciplinary action is taken,” said a civil engineering faculty member of IIT-B.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Uganda planted native trees across thousands of hectares of degraded forest; 20 years later, canopy cover and diversity reached primary forest levels
articles.summary: A forest does not recover all at once.
articles.body: A forest does not recover all at once. In Uganda's Kibale National Park, thousands of hectares of land that had been cleared for agriculture are now showing measurable signs of recovery after decades of active tree planting. A study published in Ecology and Evolution titled Chronosequence Resampling Elucidates Tree Community and Forest Structure Recovery Patterns in Restored Tropical Rainforest examined how forests changed across nearly three decades of restoration. Led by Eveliina Korkiatupa of the University of Eastern Finland, the research compared 45 actively restored forest sites ranging from four to 26 years old with 10 primary forest reference sites. The researchers used vegetation surveys conducted in 2013 and repeated in 2021 to track changes in tree diversity, forest structure and community composition. They found that after about 20 years of planting, canopy cover and Simpson's diversity had reached levels similar to those recorded in the primary forest reference sites. The recovery was far from complete, however, with several important measures of forest structure and species composition still substantially different from primary forest.The restoration effort began after decades of illegal clearingThe restoration area lies in the southern part of Kibale National Park, where approximately 10,000 to 15,000 hectares lost forest cover between the 1970s and 1990s because of illegal land clearance for agriculture. In 1994, the Uganda Wildlife Authority and Face the Future launched a reforestation project, with active restoration beginning in 1995. Restoration has since involved planting trees, removing competing grass around seedlings, preventing fires and controlling invasive species including Lantana camara. By 2023, more than 4,400 hectares had been planted with local tree species. The planting programme used a mixture of species representing different stages of forest succession. Pioneer species included Bridelia micrantha, Spathodea campanulata and Shirakiopsis elliptica, while intermediate-successional species included Albizia gummifera, Croton macrostachys, Cordia africana, Warburgia ugandensis, Mimusops bagshawei and Prunus africana. Climax species included Gambeya albida and Uvariopsis congensis. The study sites examined by Korkiatupa and her colleagues were located within these actively restored areas.Canopy cover recovered before the forest fully caught upThe clearest signs of structural recovery appeared in the canopy. The researchers found that canopy cover in restored forests reached levels similar to those of the primary forest reference sites after roughly two decades of restoration. A closing canopy can alter conditions on the forest floor by reducing the amount of light reaching competing grasses, potentially creating conditions that allow additional tree species to establish and survive. Simpson's diversity, an index that incorporates both species richness and the relative abundance of species, also reached values comparable to the primary forest after 20 years of planting. Species accumulation analyses similarly showed that the oldest restored forests had reached the primary forest's level of tree taxa richness in 2021. But this did not mean that the restored forests had become equivalent to primary forest. Overall, restored sites still had lower tree taxa richness, basal area and stem density in the statistical comparisons, while tree height also remained significantly lower. The researchers therefore described the recovery as partial, with different components of the forest developing at different speeds.Big trees are still largely missing from the restored areasOne of the biggest gaps was the number and size of large trees. In the study, trees with a diameter at breast height of at least 20 centimetres were classified as large trees, and they remained less abundant in restored forests than in primary forest even after 20 to 26 years of planting. The researchers noted that large and old trees account for much of a forest's biomass and play important roles in carbon storage, forest architecture, habitat creation and the regulation of light, moisture and other conditions beneath the canopy. Measurements of planted trees showed that they generally reached the 20-centimetre diameter threshold after approximately 14 to 21 years. That does not mean a restored forest becomes fully mature once planted trees reach this size. The researchers cited previous work suggesting that recovery of large-tree structure and associated forest functions can require one to two centuries. They also noted that the understorey and smaller tree communities can change more quickly, while the composition of medium and large trees remains much more distinct from primary forest.The species mix is changing, but full community recovery will take much longerThe restored forests were also becoming more similar to primary forest in some biological characteristics, although the overall tree community remained clearly distinct. In the 2021 survey, the proportion of shade-tolerant and forest-interior species increased along the restoration age gradient, while forest-non-dependent species were more common in restored forests than in primary forest. The researchers recorded about 60 tree taxa in the restored forests, compared with more than 350 tree species previously recorded in Kibale's primary forest, leaving substantial scope for further colonisation by later-successional species. At least four late-successional taxa had reached the restored forests after 13 to 26 years of planting, although the researchers noted that some species could have originated from planted individuals rather than arriving through dispersal from primary forest. Community composition overall remained distinct from primary forest, and the authors cited research estimating that tropical forest communities can require at least 120 years to recover 90% of reference-site values. The Kibale study therefore presents restoration as a gradual process rather than a simple return to the original forest: canopy and some measures of diversity can recover within decades, while large-tree structure and the composition of the wider tree community continue changing for much longer.You use AI every day. articles.body: The United Arab Emirates has suspended flights operated by Iranian airlines, becoming the latest country to restrict Tehran’s air links following sweeping US sanctions targeting Iran’s aviation sector.The UAE’s general civil aviation authority announced the decision on Thursday, with state news agency WAM saying all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the country had been suspended.The authority said the move was based on US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines, which prevent them from using airports around the world, as per Al Jazeera report.UAE joins growing list of countries restricting Iranian flightsThe UAE has joined Oman, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkmenistan in restricting or suspending access for Iranian airlines following the new US sanctions.Dubai is a major destination for Iranian carriers, with several daily flights between the two countries, while the UAE is also home to a large Iranian community and has close commercial ties with Iran.An Iran Airtour flight from Tehran to Dubai was cancelled shortly before its scheduled departure on Thursday morning, despite tickets having already been issued, according to AFP.US sanctions target Iran's aviation sectorThe US Treasury earlier this month imposed sweeping sanctions on Iran's aviation sector, targeting 27 airlines and dozens of companies accused of supporting them.Washington's measures are aimed at cutting off Iran's international air links. The US has warned that airports and companies continuing to service sanctioned Iranian carriers could risk losing access to the US dollar financial system.Iran has criticised the restrictions and is seeking to restore suspended routes through diplomatic and aviation talks.Iran's civil aviation organization spokesman Majid Akhavan said negotiations were under way to remove the restrictions and resume flights to the UAE.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sea bass, roasted eggplant, honey ice cream: What was on Trump-Xi dinner menu
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at a state dinner in the White
articles.body: US president Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at a state dinner in the White House’s East Room on Thursday.The dinner, held as part of Xi’s highly anticipated US visit, was prepared under Melania Trump’s direction, according to the Office of the First Lady.The menu for the dinner featured fish, fresh vegetables among other things with “American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence."“The meal begins with a toast of Schramsberg ‘Blanc De Noir,’ honoring the historic ‘Toast to Peace’ shared by President Nixon and Premier Zhou Enlai in Beijing in 1972. The same American sparkling wine served at that historic gathering continues to be enjoyed at White House functions today,” the White House said.The state dinner menu featured a mix of French-inspired and Asian-influenced dishes. The first course included yellow squash velouté and wild mushroom fricassée with crispy pancetta and scallion oil, followed by sesame-crusted sea bass with braised baby bok choy, roasted eggplant and sauce vert.Dessert featured vanilla crémeux with a sour cherry confit centre, served on walnut frangipane with White House Honey ice cream.The menu offered a departure from Trump’s reported preference for red meat and hearty salads such as Cobb or Caesar. During his March visit to Beijing, Chinese hosts similarly accommodated his tastes while incorporating local flavours, serving dishes including crispy beef ribs, roast duck, lobster in tomato soup, seasonal vegetables, salmon in mustard sauce and pan-fried pork buns, followed by tiramisu.Before the dinner, Trump and Xi exchanged warm remarks, highlighting the importance of ties between the two countries and expressing hopes for a more stable relationship. The state dinner in the White House’s East Room brought together more than 130 invited guests, including senior US officials, business leaders and executives from some of America’s leading technology companies.In his remarks, Trump acknowledged the differences between the US and Chinese political systems while stressing the enduring ties between the two peoples. The guest list featured several prominent American technology executives, while Chinese business leaders were notably absent, despite discussions between US and Chinese planners about including executives from several major Chinese companies.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: A fresh landslide in Rimbi village under the Yuksom-Tashiding constituency of West Sikkim triggered a mudslide on Friday, sending large amounts of mud, rocks and debris downhill amid continued rainfall.The landslide has raised concerns among residents as nearby houses, properties and road connectivity remain at risk. A video of the incident showed rocks, mud and debris crashing down the hillside.Last week, another landslide in Lingding, Tadong, damaged part of a house, with mud and rainwater entering rooms on the first floor. Three water pipelines were also damaged, affecting the local water supply.The road near Lingding Jhora remained inaccessible for several hours, from around 3am to 9am, before debris was cleared and traffic movement was restored. No injuries or deaths were reported in the incident.Residents moved to safer areasIn another development, 128 people from 28 houses in vulnerable areas of Rimbi in Gyalshing district were shifted to safer locations following fresh landslide activity and heavy rainfall, according to the Sikkim state disaster management authority.Relief and restoration operations were carried out in Rimbi and Singlitam, with the administration providing assistance to affected residents and clearing accumulated debris.Authorities have urged residents to stay away from active landslide zones and exercise caution as rainfall continues.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Kashmiri Pandits driven out by Pakistan-backed terrorists’: India at UN
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India on Thursday rebuked Pakistan over its remarks on Kashmir and minorities in India at the UN Human Rights Council, calling out Islamabad
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India on Thursday rebuked Pakistan over its remarks on Kashmir and minorities in India at the UN Human Rights Council, calling out Islamabad for its illegal occupation of parts of Jammu and Kashmir and demanding that it vacate them.Exercising India's right to reply to the comments made by Pakistan at the council, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi advised Islamabad to direct its energy towards a debt-ridden economy surviving on bailouts rather than harbouring territorial ambitions or sponsoring cross-border terrorism."Since Pakistan appears to need the reminder under every agenda item, Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India. The only part of Jammu and Kashmir under foreign occupation is the part Pakistan holds, which we again call upon it to vacate," Tyagi said."India is home to one of the largest Muslim populations in the world and our minorities vote, legislate, sit on a highest court and lead our institutions. In Pakistan, Hindu, Sikh and Christian communities have shrunk drastically since independence. Their daughters are abducted, forcibly converted and married off. Blasphemy laws hang over every minority household. Its own Muslim minorities, Shias, Ahmadiyyas, Ismailis and Hazaras face systemic persecution and their places of worship are attacked and desecrated," he added.Exposing this blatant double standard, Kshitij Tyagi said, "The Council does not need Pakistan to explain what happened in 1990 to the Kashmiri Pandits driven from their homes by terrorists Pakistan armed, trained and sent across the border.""Those same terrorists have since killed Kashmiris of every faith, many of them Muslim. The State that sponsored them is now asking this Council for an inquiry. The irony will not be lost on this Council," he added.Meanwhile, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal issued a stern rejection of a letter circulated by Pakistan to the UN Security Council concerning a Court of Arbitration pronouncement on the Indus Waters Treaty, castigating Islamabad for twisting international legal mechanisms.Exposing Pakistan's systemic falsehoods, Randhir Jaiswal stated, "Regarding the 'permanent court' or so-called 'Permanent Court of Arbitration', I would like to say that Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda."Reiterating India's principled and unyielding legal position, Randhir Jaiswal added, "For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally-constituted court. We see this as just another attempt by Pakistan at distorting reality. Our position on this issue is very clear and we have reiterated it several times."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why is Finland asking Musk to help Ukraine prepare for winter war against Russia?
articles.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb has urged SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink coverage into parts of Russia, saying it could help Ukraine locate
articles.body: Finnish President Alexander Stubb has urged SpaceX owner Elon Musk to expand Starlink coverage into parts of Russia, saying it could help Ukraine locate and strike Russian ballistic missile launchers.Stubb said he had appealed directly to Musk to allow Starlink to work in areas where Russian missile launchers are based, including occupied Ukrainian territory and parts of Russia. He argued that such access could help Ukraine hit the launchers before they fire missiles at Ukrainian targets."That's why ... I plead that Elon Musk would give the Ukrainians the possibility to ​use Starlink in areas where there are ballistic missile launchers, either in the occupied territory of Ukraine or in Russia ​for strategic purposes because that would save lives," Stubb said.Ukraine faces a tough winterStubb's appeal comes as Ukraine prepares for another winter of Russian attacks and faces a shortage of air defence systems.Russian ballistic missile strikes reached record levels this summer, putting further pressure on Ukraine's already limited air defence resources. Patriot systems are currently the only Ukrainian air defences capable of intercepting such missiles, but Kyiv's stocks of interceptor missiles are severely depleted.Ukrainian officials believe extending Starlink coverage into Russia could help their forces target mobile ballistic missile launchers located several hundred kilometres from the border.Musk activated Starlink over Ukraine shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. The satellite internet service has since become vital to Ukraine's battlefield communications and is also used to operate drones.Starlink, however, does not currently operate over Russian territory.Zelenskyy pushes for ceasefiresUkrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has been using the UN gathering in New York to push for ceasefires covering attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Black Sea. Russia has given no public indication that it is ready to accept such arrangements.Stubb said Ukraine needed three things ahead of winter, air defences, energy infrastructure and financial support."One is air defenses and ​even Starlink would be to ​a certain extent a good ⁠air defense there. And the second one is energy installations for the winter.""The third one is money. So those are the things that we're working on. We're working on putting up a winter package ​because I don't see the war ending, you know, before the winter."Stubb also welcomed the restart of US-led peace efforts between Russia and Ukraine, following visits by US envoys to Moscow and Kyiv in August.He said the simplest way forward would be an unconditional ceasefire, followed by negotiations on security guarantees, territory, reconstruction and compensation."I still think that the easiest solution would be to call an unconditional ceasefire, basically stop the killing, as President Trump reiterated in his speech in the UN ⁠General Assembly," ​he said.Stubb said another possibility would be to freeze the fighting along the current line of contact and establish 30-km buffer zones on both sides. If that proves impossible, he said a more limited ceasefire covering energy and grain-related targets could be considered.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: On June 4, 1977, the Los Angeles Zoo recorded a milestone in the history of mountain tapir breeding when a mountain tapir was born there, becoming the
articles.body: On June 4, 1977, the Los Angeles Zoo recorded a milestone in the history of mountain tapir breeding when a mountain tapir was born there, becoming the first of the species known to have been born in a zoo. The birth added to the zoo’s history of breeding tapirs and came as the species faced growing threats across its high-Andean range. Found in the cloud forests of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, mountain tapirs are the smallest of the four tapir species. Their populations have declined in parts of their range, with hunting and habitat destruction identified among the threats to their survival.How Los Angeles Zoo bred the first mountain tapir born in a zooAccording to the Los Angeles Zoo, a mountain tapir was born at the zoo on June 4, 1977, marking the first mountain tapir birth in a zoo. This was a separate milestone from the earlier breeding of other tapir species. The zoo also records its broader tapir-breeding history, with Brazilian, Malayan and Baird’s tapirs included among the species it successfully bred.The mountain tapir had already disappeared from parts of its high-Andean range, and the remaining populations were threatened by hunting and habitat destruction. It gives a population of fewer than 2,500 individuals and describes the need for measures to secure the species’ future.How mountain tapirs survive in the high-altitude AndesAccording to the paper published by Cambridge University Press, titled ‘The mountain tapir, endangered ‘flagship’ species of the high Andes’, the mountain tapir has woolly, longer and thicker fur than the other tapir species. The coat helps the animal remain warm in the chilly conditions of its high-altitude habitat. Mountain tapirs live in cloud forests and subtropical regions of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, according to the zoo.The species is also strongly associated with water. Mountain tapirs visit swift-flowing mountain streams to swim, wallow in mud and forage for water plants. They can remain underwater for several minutes and use their trunk-like nose in the water. The zoo lists grass, leaves and fruit among the foods they can grasp with their elongated lip.Why the endangered mountain tapir faces growing threats in the AndesThe mountain tapir is endangered, and fewer than 2,500 are estimated to remain in the wild. It lists habitat loss and fragmentation associated with poppy cultivation for the drug trade, armed conflicts in Colombia and cattle ranching among the threats facing the species. articles.title: 'Dry' Uttarakhand to cut power for up to 15 hours
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: In an unprecedented move, Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd (UPCL) invoked force majeure and imposed power cuts ranging from 35 minutes to 15
articles.body: DEHRADUN: In an unprecedented move, Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd (UPCL) invoked force majeure and imposed power cuts ranging from 35 minutes to 15 hours after deficient monsoon rainfall reduced river flows and hydropower generation, widening the gap between electricity demand and supply across the state. Heavy industries in Kumaon and Garhwal faced the longest outages on Sept 21-22, while Haldwani recorded the shortest cut of 35 minutes.UPCL managing director PC Dhyani said Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd (UJVNL) was generating substantially less power this Sept than a year earlier. “Last Sept, generation during peak hours was 1,094MW, which has come down to 912MW this year because river flows have declined,” he said, putting the average shortfall at around 170MW.UPCL put Uttarakhand’s current daily power demand at around 53 million units against supply of about 48 million units, leaving a gap that has necessitated scheduled cuts across consumer categories. The daily base load requirement in Uttarakhand is around 2,700MW, of which nearly 1,000MW is supplied by the state-owned hydropower plants, meeting around 50% of the demand. The remaining is sourced from the central grid and power exchanges, which offer power generated from different sources, including hydro, thermal and solar.Supply from the central grid has also fallen. Dhyani said peak-hour allocation dropped from 426MW last Sept to 338MW this year, while two units of THDC Ltd’s hydropower project in Tehri Garhwal remained shut because of technical problems and were expected to return to service within a month. This has affected the supply of around 100MW.Coal-supply disruptions affecting thermal plants elsewhere in the country have further tightened availability on power exchanges. “Even after offering around Rs 10 per unit on the exchange, we are able to secure only about 2% of our demand,” Dhyani said.Since Sept 19, UPCL has staggered outages by consumer category. Heavy industries in Kumaon and Garhwal faced 15-hour cuts on Sept 21-22, rural Kumaon around 2 hours 40 minutes, and rural Garhwal about three hours, while Haldwani saw cuts of about 35 minutes.With festive-season demand and Haridwar Ardh Kumbh ahead, UPCL has sought additional supply from the central grid — 100MW in Oct, 150MW in Nov, 300MW in Dec, 400MW in Jan, 300MW in Feb and 175MW in March. It has also restarted a gas-based power plant that will supply around 90MW.Dhyani said field units had been asked to postpone maintenance or carry it out during scheduled outages so consumers did not face additional disruption.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: Meet 9-year-old Vishvavardhan Sharma, who memorised Panini’s 4000 sutras at age 4 and has made Gita app that works without internet
articles.summary: Vrishvardhan Sharma is a nine-year-old currently based in Bengaluru, with family roots tracing back to Patna on his mother's side and Jaipur on his
articles.body: Vrishvardhan Sharma is a nine-year-old currently based in Bengaluru, with family roots tracing back to Patna on his mother's side and Jaipur on his father's side. What sets him apart is the sheer scale of what he has committed to memory at such a young age, not simply as recitation, but paired with grammatical understanding and meaning. At the age of five, Vrishvardhan memorised the entire Bhagavad Gita and was given the opportunity to recite it in full at Shringeri before Shankaracharya Vidhushekhar Bharati. A year later, at six, he won the National Gita Medal. Since then, he has reportedly completed more than 526 full Gita parayanas, chanting six chapters every morning while analysing each shloka grammatically.His most demanding achievement came at age eight, when he memorised the Ashtadhyayi, Panini's foundational and famously complex work on Sanskrit grammar, comprising roughly 4,000 sutras, along with the Amarkosha, a classical Sanskrit thesaurus. For this, he reportedly won a national gold medal, competing against university-level postgraduate scholars. He has also attained the status of Ghanapathi for Shri Rudram, a highly advanced and rigorous mode of Vedic chanting.From ancient grammar to self-taught computer codeWhat makes Vrishvardhan's story particularly striking is the second half of it. Alongside his classical training, he taught himself modern programming languages, including Python and C, entirely on his own. He has used these self-taught skills to build several real, functioning tools. His most notable creation is GitaVardhan, an app offering the complete Bhagavad Gita in thirteen Indian languages, featuring the commentaries of Adi Shankaracharya and Ramanujacharya. Every shloka in the app includes audio recitation in Vrishvardhan's own voice, and the app works entirely offline, is free to use, and carries no advertising or user tracking. He has also built KannadaVardhan, a tool designed to help newcomers to Bengaluru pick up spoken Kannada naturally, and has engineered a pocket-sized, voice-activated offline Gita reader device, built in two separate versions, one with an e-ink screen and one with a touchscreen, with a third version reportedly in progress. Beyond apps and devices, he has also handwritten the complete Gita in eleven different Indian scripts as a personal project dedicated to the idea of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat, or One India, Great India.Recognition beyond social mediaWhile much of Vrishvardhan's recognition has spread through viral social media posts, he has also received notable, verifiable acknowledgement. He was featured on Vaartaavali, Doordarshan's national weekly Sanskrit programme, where he was interviewed in Sanskrit, Hindi, and English. He has also appeared as a guest on The Pamphlet podcast, was welcomed by spiritual leader Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar at a felicitation event where he demonstrated his GitaVardhan app and device, and was separately felicitated on stage by the Bharatiya Janata Party's Karnataka unit for his combined work in science and scripture. His competitive track record includes a silver medal at age six at a Central Sanskrit University event held in Ayodhya, competing against university-level students, followed by another silver at Haridwar, and reportedly a first-place finish in India's Ashtadhyayi Kanthapatha recitation category at a national final held in Kanchipuram in March 2026, where he competed against participants aged eighteen to twenty-five.A rare blend of tradition and technologyVrishvardhan Sharma's story stands out not simply because of his memory or his age, but because of how deliberately he has connected two very different worlds, ancient Sanskrit scholarship and modern software engineering, using one to make the other more accessible to others. At nine years old, he is not just preserving centuries-old texts in his own memory; he is actively building tools to help other people access that same knowledge, entirely free and without needing an internet connection.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Brazilian President Lula da Silva has accused US President Donald Trump of trying to “colonise” Brazil and gain access to its natural resources by
articles.body: Brazilian President Lula da Silva has accused US President Donald Trump of trying to “colonise” Brazil and gain access to its natural resources by interfering in next month's presidential election.The accusation was made in a campaign advertisement aired by Lula's team on Thursday, as concerns grow in Brazil over alleged US attempts to influence the vote.The one-minute advert claims Trump is backing Lula's far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, because it would help advance US interests in Brazil.“Flávio Bolsonaro is Trump’s candidate and what Trump wants is to colonise Brazil, take our riches, steal our future and leave us in the dust,” the female narrator says in the video.The US State Department has rejected allegations of interference. “Any insinuation of a ‘ploy’ to undermine a democratic nation’s election is a baseless lie,” it said last month.Lula also accused Bolsonaro of seeking to transfer Brazil's natural resources to the US.“If it’s up to him, Brazil will become a colony again,” the incumbent leftwing president wrote on X.Election enters final stretchThe first round of voting is due on October 4, with Lula and Bolsonaro running close in the polls. A second round will take place on October 25 if no candidate wins more than half of the vote.The allegations come amid growing concerns in Brazil and abroad about Washington's actions towards the country. The Trump administration has applied 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports, adding to diplomatic and economic pressure between the two countries.Lula also addressed the issue at the UN General Assembly in New York this week, warning against attempts to interfere with Brazil's democratic process.“We will not allow the enemies of democracy – internal or external – to attack the will of the people. Brazilian democracy belongs to the Brazilians,” he told delegates.Earlier this week, dozens of Democratic members of Congress also accused the Trump administration of attempting to interfere in Brazil's election. In a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, they referred to an “apparent effort to interfere with, and potentially undermine” the vote through what they described as a “sustained, multifaceted campaign of interference and destabilisation in Brazil”.Claims of US pressureLula's campaign advert points to several recent reports to support its allegations. These include claims involving Big Tech companies and a confidential warning from Brazil's intelligence agency to electoral authorities about a “critical level” of risk of US interference.The advert also refers to reported links between Bolsonaro's campaign and Rockbridge, a conservative donor network co-founded by US Vice President JD Vance.Éden Valadares, communications secretary of Lula's Workers' Party, said the campaign was intended to warn Brazilians about what he called an ideologically driven US campaign.“We don’t believe it will work but nor will we sit back and do nothing,” Valadares said.“President Lula has instructed us … to mobilise Brazilian society … [and] to react in the streets,” he added, saying nationwide events were being planned for Sunday.Concerns about US influence have also been raised outside Lula's political camp. Renan Santos, another right-wing presidential candidate, criticised Trump's actions and said he did not want Brazil to become a US vassal state.“They want to interfere in Brazil’s elections to secure satisfactory contracts involving rare earths,” Santos claimed in a social media video.Recalling the US invasion of Venezuela in January, Santos added: “I don’t want to see Latin America become an American protectorate.”In their letter to Rubio, the Democratic lawmakers also accused Washington of using diplomatic, economic and political pressure in ways they said could weaken Brazil's democratic institutions and public confidence in its electoral system, while damaging ties with a major US ally and trading partner.You use AI every day. articles.summary: ROHTAK: Former Haryana chief minister and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Wednesday strongly condemned the reported lathicharge on farmers
articles.body: ROHTAK: Former Haryana chief minister and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Wednesday strongly condemned the reported lathicharge on farmers in Kurukshetra, alleging that the BJP government in the state was not working in the interests of farmers and was instead “harassing” them.Hooda said farmers were facing difficulties in selling their produce as procurement at government mandis was yet to pick up, while private buyers were purchasing the crop at significantly lower rates.“The government claims that bajra will be procured at Rs 2,900 per quintal, but procurement has not started properly. In the private market, farmers are being forced to sell it for around Rs 1,800 to Rs 1,900 per quintal,” Hooda said.He alleged that farmers were also facing difficulties in the procurement of paddy and were being forced to wait at grain markets with their produce.“Farmers are sitting distressed in the mandis because their crops are not being procured on time,” Hooda said, adding that the government needed to ensure timely procurement and payment to farmers.Strongly condemning the alleged lathicharge in Kurukshetra, Hooda said the use of force against farmers was unacceptable and accused the state government of failing to address their genuine concerns.He also alleged that farmers were not receiving essential agricultural inputs such as urea and DAP fertilisers on time, forcing them to make repeated rounds of supply centres.“This government is not farmer-friendly. Farmers are being troubled at every step. They do not get urea and DAP on time, procurement of crops is not taking place properly and they are being forced to sell their produce at lower prices in the private market,” Hooda alleged.Hooda said the government should immediately ensure uninterrupted procurement of farmers’ produce at the announced rates and make adequate supplies of fertilisers available ahead of the sowing season.His remarks came amid his ongoing public outreach in Garhi Sampla-Kiloi, where he has been meeting villagers and raising issues concerning farmers, the electoral process and the functioning of the state government.Earlier, Hooda had announced that the Haryana Congress would stage a protest outside the State Election Commission office in Chandigarh, alleging irregularities in the electoral process.Meanwhile, Rohtak Zila Parishad chairperson and BJP candidate from Garhi Sampla-Kiloi in the 2024 Haryana Assembly elections, Manju Hooda, had criticised Bhupinder Singh Hooda’s week-long public outreach in the constituency, claiming that it reflected his “weakening political hold” in the area.Manju Hooda alleged that the Congress’s support base in the constituency was declining and that the former chief minister was therefore having to reach out to voters village by village.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: From Athens to Washington: What is the ‘Thucydides Trap’ Chinese President Xi keeps invoking
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, during his meeting with US President Donald Trump, revived discussion over the “Thucydides Trap,” an idea used to describe
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping, during his meeting with US President Donald Trump, revived discussion over the “Thucydides Trap,” an idea used to describe the tensions that can arise when a rising power challenges an established one.For Xi, the message is not that conflict between China and the US is inevitable. Rather, he has repeatedly used the concept to argue that the two countries must find a way to co-exist as China’s economic, technological and military power grows.Xi also raised the same idea when Trump visited China in May.What exactly is the Thucydides Trap?The term was popularised by Harvard political scientist Graham Allison in the early 2010s. He drew on the work of Greek historian Thucydides, who wrote about the Peloponnesian War.Allison argued that history has repeatedly shown what can happen when a rising power begins to challenge an established one: the resulting tension can lead to conflict.He identified this pattern across history and used it to look at the growing rivalry between China and the US. At its simplest, the idea is about the pressure created when an emerging power starts to challenge a country that has long held the dominant position. In the case of China and the US, China's growing economic, technological and military strength has challenged America’s long-standing position as a global superpower.The concern is that even if neither country wants a confrontation, competition between the two could create tensions that become increasingly difficult to manage.From Athens and Sparta to China and the USThe concept takes its name from Thucydides, a Greek historian who lived in the 5th century BC.Thucydides described the Peloponnesian War as an inevitable clash between Athens, which was rising as a power, and Sparta, the established superpower of the time.More than two millennia later, Allison used that account to coin the term “Thucydides Trap”.Why Xi keeps using the phrase?Xi’s references to the concept go back to at least 2014, according to Zichen Wang, a Beijing-based analyst who has researched the Chinese leader’s past references to the framework.He also used the term during a meeting with US President Joe Biden in November 2024 on the sidelines of the APEC gathering in Peru.Xi’s message has remained broadly consistent: China does not see conflict as inevitable and says the two sides should find a way to live alongside each other.Beijing has often described that approach in terms of “mutual respect” and “win-win cooperation”.But the phrase also serves a broader purpose in how China presents its relationship with the US. By framing the relationship through the Thucydides Trap, Beijing places tensions over China and the US on a much wider footing than individual disputes over trade or Taiwan.It turns the relationship into a test of how two major powers can deal with each other as their interests and influence increasingly overlap.The language also underlines Beijing’s view of China as a peer of the US rather than a subordinate power. Xi put that idea directly to Trump when he asked whether the two countries could “create a new paradigm of major country relations?”US policymakers have generally been more cautious about the term. In Washington, the focus has instead tended to be on guardrails and managing risks between the two powers.Has this happened before?Allison’s research identified 16 cases over the past 500 years in which a rising power threatened to displace a dominant one. Twelve of those cases ended in war.The period leading up to World War I is one example. Germany was seeking to expand its military strength in Europe and build its own overseas empire, putting increasing pressure on its relationship with Britain, the leading power of the time.Another example is the Thirty Years’ War in the 1600s. It followed growing tensions between emerging Protestant powers, initially a group of German and Dutch states, and the established Catholic power, the Holy Roman Empire. Allison has argued that China’s growing strength could similarly challenge US influence, creating a rivalry that could eventually lead to armed conflict.The bottom lineThe historical pattern does not mean every such power transition ends in war.There have been cases where major powers have co-existed peacefully. In the last century, the US overtook the UK as the leading military and political power, and the transition was relatively smooth.Germany also regained significant power in Europe after reunifying in 1990, following its division after World War II, without triggering a conflict.The Cold War offers another example. The US and Soviet Union remained locked in a bitter rivalry, but it did not escalate into a full-scale war between the two superpowers, although they did clash through proxies.For the same reason, some analysts are still sceptical of the Thucydides Trap as a way of explaining war, arguing that the concept can oversimplify the causes of conflict and question how useful it is for understanding the relationship between China and the US.You use AI every day. articles.title: At 10, Minnesota girl Natalie Flaherty began handing out Anne Frank-inspired bracelets; two years later, 100,000 have reached all 50 states and 50+ countries, earning her a $10,000 Young Hero Prize
articles.summary: Natalie Flaherty, a Minnesota teen is one of the recipients of the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes.
articles.body: Natalie Flaherty, a Minnesota teen is one of the recipients of the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes. At just 12, the girl has been able to work towards and achieve something that generations before her struggled to. The Fairmont native founded 'I Stand With Anne', a campaign that aims to turn Holocaust remembrance into everyday action.Starting at the age of 10, Flaherty has been making bracelets that read "I Stand With Anne, Put a Stop to Hate," after reading Anne Frank's diary. She handed out her first bracelets that Halloween dressed as Anne Frank and going door to door, CBS affiliate KEYC reported. Since then, she has made 100,000 bracelets that have reached all 50 states and more than 50 countries.By 12, Flaherty has been able to work with museums, nonprofits and politicians to spread her message. She even pushed to bring a sapling of the Anne Frank chestnut tree to her hometown, which led to one being planted near Fairmont's high school. Natalie’s tree is one of only twenty Anne Frank trees planted across the country, including at the U.S. Capitol and 9/11 Memorial. In conjunction with the tree planting, she worked with local and state leaders to have May 29 declared as “Stand with Anne Day.”"It makes me feel really proud of myself," Flaherty told KEYC. She said the campaign started small and grew into something much bigger than she expected.When asked about why she wanted to apply for the prize, Flaherty said, "To get my message out there. It wasn't so much for the award as to just get my message out there.""I think the award says that she has creative, effective change. She's made a substantial impact on people in society, which is a big deal. People need it right now," said Flaherty's mother, Becky Flohrs.The Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes is a program within the Young Heroes Project non-profit organisation. Author T.A. Barron created both the program, named after his mother Gloria Barron, and the organisation in 2001. For 25 years, the program has annually recognised 25 children ages 8 to 18 years old from the United States and Canada who possess leadership qualities and are individually instrumental in bringing a positive impact on fellow people, communities and environments.Flaherty was among the entrants last year as well. It was recommended by an organisation she worked with previously, which brought it to her attention. She decided to apply again this year. "When we researched the program, it made a lot of sense that she would apply for it," Flohrs said.Application submissions open in January, and winners are revealed in September. To apply, Flaherty wrote essays describing her work, what she had learned, what it impacted, what she will do in the future and submitted three letters of recommendation. "I was happy when I completed it," Flaherty recalled.According to barronprize.org, a panel of 10 selected independent contest judges determine 25 potential finalists, 10 potential runner-up prize winners and 15 potential grand prize winners based on their criteria, including entrants leading, organising, or initiating a beneficial non-school, non-work project and demonstrating positive qualities.Flaherty and Flohrs were contacted by the organisation and discovered that Flaherty won the prize, among 2,000 applicants, recognising her for distributing more than 100,000 "I Stand with Anne, Put a Stop to Hate" bracelets worldwide. They shared the news on Tuesday, September 15. They recounted that the discovery was an emotional one. "Me and my mom were crying when we found out because it was just so exciting," said Flaherty."They emailed us and said, 'Hey, we want to talk, nothing bad, you don't need to prepare anything', which means we prepared everything," Flohrs added with a laugh. "We thought they needed more information on her application and they said, 'I'm sure you know why I'm calling', and we were like, 'We have no idea why you're calling', and they let us know that she had won, and she was going to send the winners’ information over."All 25 winners receive a custom plaque and certificate. The top 15 winners are awarded $10,000, which may be used for public service efforts or further education. Flaherty received the plaque, certificate, prize money, and one of T.A. Barron's books, "The Hero's Trail," on Thursday, September 17. "I feel very accomplished and very grateful for everyone who has helped me along with this mission," Flaherty said.Now, Flaherty plans to invest, set her bracelet distribution back in motion, save for post-secondary school and make donations. In the future, she plans to continue working with educators and politicians on educational reform addressing hate and how to challenge it.With the Kindness Club, she plans to distribute bracelets on Halloween once more with the "Wicked" theme. She said people can rally behind and support "I Stand with Anne, Put a Stop to Hate" by choosing kindness and knowledge."It says that they also have the same idea as me, and they also don't want hate to have a ripple effect and break our world," Flaherty said. "Wear the bracelet, t-shirt and say kind and good words. Embody it."The "I Stand with Anne, Put a Stop to Hate" bracelets have been distributed for free and are available at the Anne Frank Centre USA, the Holocaust Museum and select businesses in the Fairmont area. Shirts are available at annefrank.com.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Gyanesh Kumar hatao, EC bachao': Congress puts up posters targeting CEC in Delhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday upped the ante against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and put up posters demanding his removal in Delhi amid the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday upped the ante against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and put up posters demanding his removal in Delhi amid the ongoing row over the functioning of the poll panel and Special Intensive Revision of electoral list.Put up by the Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee's OBC department, the poster read, "Remove Gyanesh Kumar, save Election Commission."This came a day after Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at Gyanesh Kumar after reports of differences within the poll body over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls sparked a political stir.Rahul accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation"."The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference."I come from a political family, and I have spent more than 50 years in a political family... In India, there is a fundamental force called anti-incumbency that very quickly starts to resist any government. It does not spare anybody. Indira Gandhi won the Bangladesh war, was at the height of her popularity, and then suddenly, within a year or two, massive anti-incumbency, massive pressure," he added.Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed outside the Election Commission office in Delhi ahead of a protest demonstration by Delhi Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.The Indian Youth Congress is also scheduled to hold a protest march from 5, Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar on Friday, demanding the resignation of Kumar.The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Thursday also launched a nationwide online citizens' petition titled "Gyanesh, It's Done Bro", seeking action against the CEC and calling upon citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability.An Indian Express report has highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls. The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.The Election Commission, however, described the queries and observations raised by its members as part of its routine internal process. It said written notes, technical inputs and internal scrutiny were standard mechanisms to check legal compliance and protect voters' rights.The ECI further said all decisions taken by the Commission, including those related to SIR, had full legal backing and stressed that its final decisions were unanimous.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
